Definition: from G2233; a leader, i.e. chief person (or figuratively, place) of a province:--governor, prince, ruler.
BiblicalUsage: A hegemon is a ruler, a governor, the one in charge, and the Gospels put the word on both the child and his judge. In Matthew 2:6 a governor shall come out of Bethlehem to rule Israel, in Matthew 27:11 Jesus stands before the governor and is asked, art thou the King of the Jews, in Luke 20:20 the spies hope to deliver him to the governor, and in Acts 23:24 Paul is sent to Felix the governor.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the contrast is deliberate: the true Governor is the child of Bethlehem, and the men who hold the title are the ones who condemn him. Earthly rulers come and go, and the child rules them all.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
